 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.557 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Vatakara,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 05/11/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 08/11/2016 at about 03:15 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-56-B-7233 near the place by name Chilambavalav at Perambra, bus bearing registration no.KL-18-D-1988 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.

Prakasan vs Rajeevan on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110475256/
2
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver filed joined written statement denying negligence on the part of the latter.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending bus.
The age, occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A11 series and Ext.C1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral evidence was adduced by the respondents.
Ext. B1
was produced by the third respondent.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending bus resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 18,50,600/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has 2025:KER:73489 come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner-
Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a businessman, was earning 30,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 10,000/-, which is on the lower side and so the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal is reasonable and if at all the Court is inclined to enhance it, the same may be as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are no materials on record to prove the claim 2025:KER:73489 regarding the income.
However, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra) the income of a coolie in the year 2016 is liable to be fixed as 10,500/-.

In the absence of any better materials on record to prove the income,
the income of the claim petitioner herein can also be fixed as 10,500/-.
Loss of earnings 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"1. Global brachial plexes injury right upper limb post traumatic.
2. Fracture transverse process of C5, C6.
Prakasan vs Rajeevan on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110475256/
3 3.
Fracture body of scapula.
4. Fracture second rib."
He was hospitalized for a period of 48 days.
In all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 8 months.

Hence, he can be awarded compensation for a period of 8 months, that is,
10,500/-x8 months= 84,000/-.
Addition to be made towards future prospects 11.
The claim petitioner was 45 years old at the time of the accident.
The functional disability has been fixed as 80%.
Therefore 25% of his income is liable to be added towards his established income as loss of future prospects.
12. The learned counsel for the claim petitioner canvasses for enhancement of compensation under the other heads also.
However, on going through the impugned Award, I find that reasonable amounts have been awarded and so, no interference into the same is called for.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 4,43,984/- (total compensation =22,94,584/- that is, 18,50,600/- granted by the Tribunal +
4,43,984/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization (excluding the period of 176 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.

The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the 2025:KER:73489 compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
